items.title: Work Done
items.body: \(W=Fd\cos\theta\) where \(F\) is force, \(d\) distance, \(\theta\) angle between force and displacement. Units: Joules (J).

items.title: Potential Energy
items.body: Gravitational PE: \(GPE=mgh\). Change in GPE: \(\Delta GPE=mg\Delta h\).

items.title: Power
items.body: \(P=\dfrac{W}{t}=Fv\). Units: Watts (W). Maximum speed when driving force = resistance: \(P=F_{resistance}\cdot v_{max}\).

body.en: Kinetic energy: \(\text{KE}=\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\). Gravitational PE: \(\text{GPE}=mgh\). Work-energy principle: net work done = change in KE. Work done by a force: \(W=Fd\cos\theta\). Power: \(P=\dfrac{W}{t}=Fv\). Conservation of energy: \(\text{KE}_1+\text{GPE}_1=\text{KE}_2+\text{GPE}_2\) (no friction).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Energy, Work & Power

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

caption.ar: تمثيل بياني إحداثي يوضح سلوك الدالة والخصائص التحليلية المحورية في الشغل والطاقة والقدرة الميكانيكية. \(KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\) ، \(2\text{ kg}\)

body.en:
Double-counting gravity: In energy equations, you either account for gravity through Gravitational Potential Energy (\(\Delta KE + \Delta PE = W_{\text{external}}\)) OR through work done by gravity (\(\Delta KE = W_g + W_{\text{friction}} + \dots\)). Including both simultaneously counts gravitational work twice.

Driving force vs Net force in \(P = Fv\): The force in \(P = Fv\) is the tractive/driving force produced by the engine, NOT the resultant force. At maximum or steady velocity, acceleration is zero, so the driving force exactly equals the total opposing resistance (\(F_{\text{drive}} = R + mg\sin\alpha\)).

Work against friction: Work done against friction is \(W = F \times d\) (where \(d\) is the distance along the surface). This mechanical energy converts irreversibly into heat.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Energy, Work & Power)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

problem.en: A 2 kg ball rolls down a smooth slope of height 5 m from rest. Find its speed at the bottom (\(g=10\) m/s²).

solution.en: \[\text{Loss in GPE}=\text{Gain in KE}:\quad2\times10\times5=\tfrac{1}{2}\times2\times v^2\Rightarrow v^2=100\Rightarrow v=10\text{ m/s}.\]

problem.en: A car of mass 900 kg moves at constant speed 30 m/s against a resistance of 500 N. Find the power output of the engine.

solution.en:
At constant speed, driving force = resistance = 500 N.

\[P=Fv=500\times30=15\,000\text{ W}=15\text{ kW}.\]

label.en: Worked Example — Work-Energy Principle on a Rough Horizontal Plane
label.ar: مثال محلول — مبدأ الشغل والطاقة على مستوى أفقي خشن

problem.en: A block of mass \(4\text{ kg}\) slides across a rough horizontal floor with initial speed \(6\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and comes to rest after travelling \(9\text{ m}\). Take \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Using the work-energy principle, find the coefficient of friction \(\mu\).
problem.ar: ينزلق جسم كتلته \(4\text{ kg}\) على أرضية أفقية خشنة بسرعة ابتدائية \(6\text{ m s}^{-1}\) ويتوقف بعد قطع مسافة \(9\text{ m}\). اعتبر \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\). باستعمال مبدأ الشغل والطاقة أوجد معامل الاحتكاك \(\mu\).

solution.en:
Initial kinetic energy: \(\text{KE}_i = \frac{1}{2}(4)(6^2) = 72\text{ J}\). Final kinetic energy is \(0\).

The normal reaction is \(R = mg = 40\text{ N}\), so the constant friction force is \(F = 40\mu\). Work done against friction over \(9\text{ m}\) is \(W_f = 9 \times 40\mu = 360\mu\).

Equating energy loss to work against friction: \(360\mu = 72 \implies \mu = 0.2\).
solution.ar:
طاقة الحركة الابتدائية: \(\frac{1}{2}(4)(36) = 72\text{ J}\) والنهائية صفر.

ردّ الفعل العمودي \(R = 40\text{ N}\)، وقوة الاحتكاك \(40\mu\)، والشغل المبذول ضد الاحتكاك خلال \(9\text{ m}\) هو \(360\mu\).

إذن \(360\mu = 72 \implies \mu = 0.2\).

label.en: Worked Example — Maximum Speed of a Vehicle on a Slope
label.ar: مثال محلول — السرعة القصوى لمركبة على منحدر

problem.en: A van of mass \(1500\text{ kg}\) has an engine working at a maximum power of \(45\text{ kW}\) as it climbs a straight road inclined at angle \(\alpha\) where \(\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{15}\). If constant non-gravitational resistance is \(620\text{ N}\), take \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) and find the maximum steady speed up the road.
problem.ar: شاحنة كتلتها \(1500\text{ kg}\) يعمل محركها بقدرة قصوى \(45\text{ kW}\) أثناء صعودها طريقاً مستقيماً يميل بزاوية \(\alpha\) حيث \(\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{15}\). إذا كانت المقاومة الثابتة غير الجاذبية \(620\text{ N}\) فاعتبر \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) وأوجد أقصى سرعة منتظمة صعوداً.

solution.en:
At maximum speed \(v_{\max}\), acceleration \(a = 0\), so driving force equals total opposing force:

\[D = R_{\text{res}} + mg\sin\alpha = 620 + 1500(9.8)\left(\frac{1}{15}\right) = 620 + 980 = 1600\text{ N}.\]

Using \(P = Dv_{\max}\) with \(P = 45\,000\text{ W}\):

\[v_{\max} = \frac{45\,000}{1600} = 28.125\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 28.1\text{ m s}^{-1}.\]
solution.ar:
عند السرعة القصوى \(v_{\max}\) يكون التسارع صفراً: \[D = 620 + 1500(9.8)\left(\frac{1}{15}\right) = 620 + 980 = 1600\text{ N}.\]

وباستعمال \(P = Dv_{\max}\): \[v_{\max} = \frac{45\,000}{1600} = 28.125\text{ m s}^{-1}.\]

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Energy, Work & Power)

rows.en: The \(25\%\) reduction applies to the larger base \(1.25 Q_0\), not \(Q_0\).
Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Energy, Work & Power

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: A car of mass \(1200\text{ kg}\) ascends a hill of inclination \(\alpha\), where \(\sin\alpha = \tfrac{1}{20}\), against a constant resistance to motion of \(500\text{ N}\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): (a) find the driving force required to travel at a steady speed of \(25\text{ m/s}\), (b) calculate the power developed by the engine in kilowatts.

solution.en: (a) Component of weight down the slope: \[W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = 1200(9.8)\left(\tfrac{1}{20}\right) = 60(9.8) = 588\text{ N}\] Since the car travels at steady speed (acceleration \(a = 0\)), the engine driving force balances all resistance: \[F_{\text{drive}} = \text{Resistance} + mg\sin\alpha = 500 + 588 = 1088\text{ N}\] (b) Power output: \[P = F_{\text{drive}} \times v = 1088 \times 25 = 27\,200\text{ W} = 27.2\text{ kW}\]

hints.en: (a) Component of weight down the slope: \(W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = 1200(9.8)\left(\tfrac{1}{20}\right) = 60(9.8)\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = 1200(9.8)\left(\tfrac{1}{20}\right) = 60(9.8)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Since the car travels at steady speed (acceleration \(a = 0\)), the engine driving force balances all resistance: \(F_{\text{drive}} = \text{Resistance} + mg\sin\alpha = 500 + 588\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a = 0\) ، \(F_{\text{drive}} = \text{Resistance} + mg\sin\alpha = 500 + 588\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(P = F_{\text{drive}} \times v = 1088 \times 25\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: A block of mass \(5\text{ kg}\) is released from rest at the top of a rough plane inclined at \(30^\circ\) to the horizontal. The length of the incline is \(8\text{ m}\) and the coefficient of friction is \(\mu = 0.2\). Using the work-energy principle and taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\), calculate the speed of the block at the bottom of the incline.

solution.en:
1. Vertical height descended: \(h = 8\sin 30^\circ = 8(0.5) = 4\text{ m}\).
Initial gravitational potential energy: \[\text{PE} = mgh = 5(9.8)(4) = 196\text{ J}\] 2. Normal reaction: \(R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 5(9.8)\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 24.5\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\).
Friction force: \(F = \mu R = 0.2(24.5\sqrt{3}) = 4.9\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\).
Work done against friction over distance \(d = 8\text{ m}\): \[W_{\text{fric}} = F \times d = (4.9\sqrt{3}) \times 8 = 39.2\sqrt{3} \approx 67.896\text{ J}\] 3. By work-energy principle: \[\text{Gain in KE} = \text{Loss in PE} - W_{\text{fric}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = 196 - 67.896 = 128.104\text{ J}\] Substitute \(m = 5\text{ kg}\): \[2.5v^2 = 128.104 \Rightarrow v^2 = \dfrac{128.104}{2.5} = 51.2416 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{51.2416} \approx 7.16\text{ m/s (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(h = 8\sin 30^\circ = 8(0.5)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Initial gravitational potential energy: \(\text{PE} = mgh = 5(9.8)(4) = 196\text{ J}\) Normal reaction: \(R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 5(9.8)\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\text{PE} = mgh = 5(9.8)(4) = 196\text{ J}\) ، \(R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 5(9.8)\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] A constant force of 15 N is applied to an object, causing it to move a distance of 4 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done by the force.

hints.en: The work done by a constant force is given by the formula: Work Done = Force × Distance × cos(θ).
Where θ is the angle between the force and the direction of motion. In this case, the force and the distance are in the same direction, so θ = 0°. Therefore, cos(0°) = 1. Work Done = 15 N × 4 m × 1.
Substitute the simplified values from the previous step to complete the calculation.

solution.en:
The work done by a constant force is given by the formula:
Work Done = Force × Distance × cos(θ)
where θ is the angle between the force and the direction of motion.
In this case, the force and the distance are in the same direction, so θ = 0°.
Therefore, cos(0°) = 1.
Work Done = 15 N × 4 m × 1
Work Done = 60 J

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A stone of mass \(0.5\text{ kg}\) is projected vertically upwards with speed \(14\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) and neglecting air resistance, use conservation of mechanical energy to find the maximum height reached.
question.ar: [تدريب 4 · متوسط] يُقذف حجر كتلته \(0.5\text{ kg}\) رأسياً إلى أعلى بسرعة \(14\text{ m s}^{-1}\). باعتبار \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) وإهمال مقاومة الهواء، استعمل حفظ الطاقة الميكانيكية لإيجاد أقصى ارتفاع يصل إليه.

hints.en: At maximum height, the velocity is zero so all initial kinetic energy has converted to gravitational potential energy.
hints.ar: عند أقصى ارتفاع تنعدم السرعة وتتحول كل طاقة الحركة الابتدائية إلى طاقة وضع جاذبية.

hints.en: Set \(\frac{1}{2}mu^2 = mgh\), noting that mass \(m\) cancels cleanly.
hints.ar: ضع \(\frac{1}{2}mu^2 = mgh\) ولاحظ اختصار الكتلة \(m\) من الطرفين.

solution.en: By conservation of mechanical energy: \(\frac{1}{2}(0.5)(14^2) = (0.5)(9.8)h \implies h = \frac{196}{19.6} = 10\text{ m}\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Hard] A cyclist and bicycle of combined mass \(80\text{ kg}\) travel up a slope inclined at \(\theta\) where \(\sin\theta = \frac{1}{20}\) at a constant speed of \(6\text{ m s}^{-1}\). If the cyclist develops a useful power of \(480\text{ W}\), take \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\) and find the magnitude of the constant resistance force opposing the motion.
question.ar: [تدريب 5 · صعب] يصعد راكب دراجة مع دراجته بكتلة كلية \(80\text{ kg}\) منحدراً يميل بزاوية \(\theta\) حيث \(\sin\theta = \frac{1}{20}\) بسرعة ثابتة \(6\text{ m s}^{-1}\). إذا كانت القدرة المفيدة المبذولة \(480\text{ W}\) وباعتبار \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\)، فأوجد مقدار قوة المقاومة الثابتة المعاكسة للحركة.

hints.en: Use \(P = Dv\) to find the driving force \(D = \frac{480}{6}\) exerted by the cyclist.
Because the speed is constant (\(a = 0\)), \(D = mg\sin\theta + R_{\text{res}}\).
hints.ar: بما أن السرعة ثابتة (\(a = 0\)) فإن \(D = mg\sin\theta + R_{\text{res}}\).

hints.en: Calculate \(mg\sin\theta = 80(10)\left(\frac{1}{20}\right) = 40\text{ N}\) and subtract from \(D = 80\text{ N}\).

solution.en:
Driving force: \(D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{480}{6} = 80\text{ N}\).

Since speed is constant: \(D = mg\sin\theta + R_{\text{res}} \implies 80 = 80(10)\left(\frac{1}{20}\right) + R_{\text{res}} = 40 + R_{\text{res}}\). Hence \(R_{\text{res}} = 40\text{ N}\).
solution.ar:
قوة الدفع: \(D = \frac{480}{6} = 80\text{ N}\).

ولأن السرعة ثابتة: \(80 = 40 + R_{\text{res}} \implies R_{\text{res}} = 40\text{ N}\).
